explanation: Push new items to an input stack. When the output stack is empty, transfer all input items into it; this reverses their order once.
correctness: The output stack top is always the oldest remaining item. Transfer is performed only when it is empty, so newer items never pass older ones. Each item is moved at most once.
walkthrough: Enqueue 4 and 9 into the incoming stack. The first Dequeue moves them to the outgoing stack and removes 4. Enqueue 2 without moving the still-pending 9. The next Dequeue removes 9; only then does transferring the incoming stack expose 2. The returned values are 4, 9 and 2 in FIFO order.
timeComplexity: O(1) amortized time per operation, O(m) total for m operations.
spaceComplexity: O(q) space for q queued items.
